chunks: Muhammad ibn Ya'qub narrated from a number of our companions, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from al-Barqi, from Sa'dan, from Abdillah ibn Sinan, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said:
Whoever prays four rak'ahs, reciting 'Qul Huwa Allahu Ahad' fifty times in each rak'ah, will not depart [from this world] and there is no sin between him and Allah.

key_terms.قُلْ هُوَ اللَّهُ أَحَدٌ: Qul Huwa Allahu Ahad (Surah Al-Ikhlas, 'Say, He is Allah, the One')
key_terms.لَمْ يَنْفَتِلْ: He will not depart (die/leave the world)

ai.seo_question: What is the reward for reciting Surah Al-Ikhlas fifty times in each rak'ah of prayer?
ai.summary: Recorded in Shaykh al-Tusi’s *Tahdhib al-Ahkam*, this hadith from Imam al-Sadiq (AS) prescribes a specific voluntary prayer where Surah Al-Ikhlas is recited fifty times per rak'ah, promising that the practitioner will not depart with any outstanding sins. This practice is often linked to the broader tradition of *Salat al-Tasbih*, emphasizing the power of consistent dhikr and the specific merit of the 'Oneness of God' chapter in expiating minor sins. The phrase 'did not depart' implies a state of spiritual readiness and divine mercy at the time of death.
